'''''Malvaviscus penduliflorus''''' is a flowering plant in the family [[Malvaceae]]. It can be found in many tropical places including in the United States,<ref>{{Cite web |title=USDA Plants Database |url=https://plants.usda.gov/home/plantProfile?symbol=MAPE3 |access-date=2024-03-12 |website=plants.usda.gov}}</ref> South America, Asia, Australia, and several islands.<ref name="Rojas-Sandoval-2022">{{Cite report |title=Malvaviscus penduliflorus (Turk's cap mallow) |last=Rojas-Sandoval |first=Julissa |date=2022-01-07 |doi=10.1079/cabicompendium.86508374 |language=en|doi-access=free }}</ref>

It's known by many names including '''mazapan''', '''Turk's cap mallow''', '''cardinal's hat''', '''firecracker hibiscus''', '''sleeping hibiscus''', and '''sleepy mallow''';<ref name="GS">{{Cite web |title=Turk's Cap Mallow – University of Florida, Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences |url=https://gardeningsolutions.ifas.ufl.edu/plants/ornamentals/turks-cap.html |access-date=2024-03-12 |website=gardeningsolutions.ifas.ufl.edu}}</ref><ref name="AFP">{{Cite web |title=Malvaviscus penduliflorus – Species Details |url=http://florida.plantatlas.usf.edu/plant.aspx?id=265 |access-date=2024-03-12 |website=Atlas of Florida Plants}}</ref> some of these names are shared with other flowers, most especially ''[[Malvaviscus arboreus]]''. Its name ''penduliflorus'' means "hanging flower"<ref>{{Citation |title=penduliflorus |date=2022-12-01 |work=Wiktionary, the free dictionary |url=https://en.wiktionary.org/w/index.php?title=penduliflorus&oldid=70188138 |access-date=2024-03-12 |language=en}}</ref>

It is widely cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]], though it can also be eaten.

== Description ==
It is a perennial shrub that can reach up to {{cvt|3|–|4|m}} tall.<ref name="GS" /><ref name="NTBG">{{Cite web |title=National Tropical Botanical Garden {{!}} Malvaviscus penduliflorus – Plant Detail – Tropical Plants Database |url=https://ntbg.org/ |access-date=2024-03-15 |website=National Tropical Botanical Garden |language=en-US}}</ref> It produces red hanging tubular flowers with stamens that stick out. It has pointed, ovular leaves and hairy stems.<ref name="NTBG" /> Like other members the ''Malvaviscus'' genus, ''M. penduliflorus'' produces sap and small red fruits.

== Distribution ==
It is unknown where ''Malvaviscus penduliflorus'' is native to, though speculated to be Mexico,<ref name="Rojas-Sandoval-2022" /><ref name="GS" /> possibly as a cultivation of ''M. arboreus''.<ref name="NTBG" /> It is cultivated and naturalized throughout tropical climates including North and South America, Oceania including Australia and New Zealand, Africa, Asia, and some islands.<ref name="Rojas-Sandoval-2022" />
